findings.description: mark_invalid writes the invalid record into the file for impression.served_at.date(), and for_day builds its invalid set only from that day's file. This works only if the impression passed to refund() carries the original served_at. Correctness depends on the caller preserving that timestamp. If the impression was re-created with a different timestamp, the marker lands in the wrong file and the refund is silently ignored, so the campaign stays overcharged.
findings.suggestion: Validate that the impression was actually appended (or look up its original served_at by id) before writing the marker. Alternatively, store invalid markers in a day-independent file.
findings.title: Invalid markers are written to the file of the served day, but the refund day may differ

findings.description: can_bid calls self.spend, which calls log.for_day. That opens and JSON-parses the entire day file for the campaign. eligible() does this for every campaign on every bid request, so each request costs O(campaigns x file size), and the cost grows through the day as the file grows. The removed in-memory counters made this O(1).
findings.suggestion: Keep cached per-campaign hourly spend in memory, rebuilt from the log on startup and updated in record/refund.
findings.title: Every bid check re-reads and parses the whole day's log file
